claims.statement: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in drug discovery has profoundly transformed the pharmaceutical landscape by significantly accelerating the identification of potential drug candidates.
Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have proven to be particularly effective in modeling molecular structures, optimizing drug‑target interactions, and enhancing prediction accuracy.
GNNs offer advantages over traditional molecular representations in drug discovery.
Graph neural networks can be applied to drug discovery.
Graph Neural Networks are used in modern AI-aided drug discovery.
Graph Neural Networks can be applied to drug discovery.
An integrated decision support pipeline based on Graph Neural Networks has been developed for drug discovery.
Graph neural networks can be used for automated de novo drug design.

gaps.description: The literature lacks any empirical studies on molecular property prediction (e.g., solubility, toxicity, bioactivity) using GNNs.
There is an absence of systematic methodological comparisons or ablation studies across GNN variants (MPNN, GCN, GAT, Graph Transformers).
No work has been reported on protein–ligand interaction modeling and binding affinity prediction with GNNs.
